title: Take an anterior nasal swab on a training head: whole tip in, 4 pressed circles per nostril, cap home
instruction: Take an anterior nasal swab from both nostrils of the training head with the swab in the tube: put the whole foam tip in each nostril and rub it round the inside wall at least 4 times, then put the swab back in its tube and push the cap home.
context: CDC guidance for an anterior nasal (nares) specimen: insert the entire collection tip of the swab inside the nostril (usually 1 to 1.5 cm), firmly sample the nasal wall by rotating the swab in a circular path against it at least 4 times, about 15 seconds, then repeat in the other nostril with the same swab. Hologic's swab collection instructions warn that twirling the swab against one part of the inside of the nose is not proper technique. The swab goes back into its tube and the cap is pushed home while the other hand holds the tube. Done by: medical assistants (O*NET 31-9092.00, whose tasks include collecting laboratory specimens; 833,900 US jobs in 2025, BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook) and nurses, who also swab the anterior nares to screen for MRSA on hospital admission. Most medical assistants work in physicians' offices (BLS OEWS industry profile), where nasal swabs for flu, COVID-19 and RSV tests are routine; for send-out PCR the swab goes back into its dry transport tube.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left); heights above the table. Nasal-swab practice head (printed PLA shell; simplified face, adult-size nose and nostrils), fixed to the table (1.5 kg in simulation; the printed shell is about 0.65 kg of PLA), lying face up with the crown away from the robot: 22 cm long (x 26 to 48), 15 cm wide (y -12.5 to 2.5), 17.1 cm high at the nose tip. The eyes, brows, lips and ears are non-colliding visual details and are not part of the printable mesh. Two nostrils open on the underside of the nose toward the chin, centred at x 33, y -5.7 (the patient's left, on the robot's right) and y -4.3, 15.6 cm above the table; each is an elliptical bore 1.4 cm long and 1.0 cm wide, 2.6 cm deep, whose axis runs into the nose toward the crown, 30 degrees below horizontal. Swab (Puritan 25-1506 1PF BT BL style, blue cap; 5 g): white polystyrene shaft 0.26 cm thick, foam tip 0.48 cm across and 1.6 cm long, attached to the tube's blue cap (grip 1.3 cm across and 2.5 cm long, plug 1.0 cm across); 15.19 cm overall. Transport tube with its grey stand (one free 100 g piece): clear polypropylene tube 1.4 cm across outside and 1.12 cm inside (estimated), 16.5 cm long (Puritan's is 15.4 cm; a spacer at the stand's end stop puts its mouth at the same place, see README), lying along y at x 20 with its axis 3 cm above the table, its mouth at y -13 (toward the robot's right) and its closed end at y 3.5; the stand is a 5 cm wide plate under it (y -12.5 to 4.6) with two saddles and an end stop. The swab lies in the tube, tip first, with its plug-style cap in place as shipped: the plug in the mouth and the grip outside (centred at y -14.25).
scoring: Every step, from poses, finger-pad points and the PhysX contact points (with per-point normal forces) between the swab and the head and between the swab and the tube; the score at the end counts. For each nostril, the tip is at sampling depth when its centre is 0.8 to 1.7 cm in along the nostril's axis (the whole 1.6 cm tip inside, its end no deeper than 2.5 cm) and within the opening; a step there is pressed when the tip's contact force on that nostril's wall is at least 0.2 N (about 20 g, the press the real trial's calibrated ink needs). Circles: the larger of the signed angle the tip's centre travels round the nostril's axis over consecutive pressed steps (measured on the ellipse, 360 degrees = once round; a move of more than 90 degrees between steps does not count; when the tip is pressed again after a lift, the angle from the last pressed step counts too if it is 90 degrees or less, so an unpressed return cancels its stroke) and the laps, one each time all twelve 30-degree sectors of the wall have been pressed since the last lap, in either direction (sectors swept between consecutive pressed steps up to 90 degrees apart count; a jump of more than 90 degrees after a lift starts a new lap); steps with the tip's centre less than a quarter of the way from the axis to the wall are not used, for circles or sectors. Share: pressed steps over steps at sampling depth. Moving pressed steps: pressed steps in which the tip moved at least 1 degree round the wall. Sectors: the twelve 30-degree sectors of the wall pressed at least once. Nostril credit = min(circles, 4)/4 x min(1, share/0.7) x min(1, moving pressed steps/200) x min(1, sectors/10). Cap home: after the whole swab has been out of the tube, the cap seated on the mouth (grip within 1.5 mm of it, the swab within 6 degrees of the tube's axis and its cap within 3 mm of the axis) and pushed with at least 2 N on 5 consecutive steps (0.25 s) while a finger pad of the other hand is on the tube (within 1.2 cm of its outside; a free tube slides away, and the compliant simulated arm passes only 2 to 3.5 N through a pinched tube), then let go (no finger pad within 1.5 cm of the cap). Real trial: the cap flush on the rim (photo), pushed while the other hand holds the tube (video), which takes the real cap's full push; Puritan publishes no push force, so push one cap home on a tube standing on a 5 kg / 1 g kitchen scale before the trials and record it (a reclosable cap closed by hand is well within the YAM's ~40 N per finger). Score: the mean of the two nostril credits, times 1.0 if the cap is home, else 0.4 (an unsealed specimen). 1.0: both nostrils with at least 4 circles, a share of at least 0.7 and at least 200 moving pressed steps (10 s) and at least 10 sectors, and the cap home and let go; the run is a success (and ends) once the cap has stayed home 9 s. 0 (voided swab): the foam tip touches anything other than the insides and rims of the nostrils (rims: up to 0.8 cm outside the openings and within 1.6 times their half-widths) and the inside of the tube with at least 0.05 N (the face, the lips, the tube's or stand's outside, the table); a finger pad comes within 2 mm of the foam while the tip is outside the tube; the tip's end goes deeper than 2.5 cm; or the swab is dropped (its cap's centre lower than 1.2 cm while not held and not in the tube). A wall force above 5 N is reported, not scored (no real trial can read it).
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed in simulation. Put the swab back in its tube with the cap in place as shipped, and the stand back with the mouth toward the robot's right. Real trials: a new sterile swab per trial (single use); wipe the printed nostrils clean, re-ink them with black dry-erase marker (two coats, 2 min drying; repeat the 20 g / 5 g stroke test) and renew the green marker on the lip and skin (see README).
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The head is one fixed triangle-mesh shell; the face is simplified, while the nostrils have adult anterior-nares size and angle (each bore's floor opens toward the lip for its first ~1.3 cm). Foam tip and shaft are rigid (a real 2.5 mm polystyrene shaft bends, so a real press needs more cap travel); the press comes from the arm's compliance. Cap: seated and pushed >= 2 N for 0.25 s, other hand on the tube (no friction fit; the real cap needs its full push). Swab mass estimated.
